scope: Every current skipped/failed case plus missing local-commit cells and earlier Turso failures: 29 client/case entries. Immutable trial statuses remain unchanged. Repaired cases have explicit publication or development dispositions below.
policy: Benchmark SDK-native features only; do not implement application-owned substitutes for absent features. Missing adapters, inconvenient runtime choices and setup failures are work to do, not product limitations. Only a documented lack of an equivalent workload or an inapplicable milestone justifies omission.

cases.label: No equivalent
cases.reason: The pinned local sync server exposes database replication, not per-actor row revocation while retaining other actors and server data. Lazy page fetching is not authorization filtering.
cases.nextStep: Keep this exact native revocation contract unavailable. Database-per-user or an application purge would change the contract and must be a separately labeled workload.

cases.label: Not measured
cases.reason: The adapter deliberately disables localCommit even though the collection exposes the optimistic local update; that is not a durable queue receipt.
cases.nextStep: Measure a local-visible milestone consistently for all clients, or use the durable native executor/storage path for local commit. Never use isPersisted, which includes remote settlement, as local-only time.

cases.label: Not reached
cases.reason: Cold 100k startup exceeded 90 seconds; warm startup was never reached.
cases.nextStep: Run warm and cold as independent cases. Diagnose count-query materialization, ingestion and retained server history before changing a uniform deadline.

cases.label: Did not converge
cases.reason: Writer and other clients disagree after acknowledged writes and a 90-second deadline.
cases.nextStep: Trace the target tombstone, reconnection and native subscriptions. Retain failure until all clients agree; do not force an assumed winner.

cases.label: Purge timed out
cases.reason: The 60,000 ms purge deadline expires: online queries hide revoked rows but local storage retains them; reconnect also leaves queries stale. Fresh-client authorization passes.
cases.nextStep: Separate query visibility from native purge, and investigate reconnect/subscription behavior. Keep the observed failure, not a skipped case.
